summary.text: A ribosome is a particle found in most cells that builds proteins by reading genetic information encoded in messenger RNA (mRNA).
It links amino acids into a polypeptide chain, with transfer RNA (tRNA) bringing the correct amino acid for each codon in the mRNA.
Each ribosome has a small and a large subunit made of ribosomal RNA and proteins, and the ribosomal RNA does the work of linking the amino acids.

facts.label: Nobel Prize in 1974
facts.value: Awarded for the discovery of the ribosome

items.prompt: A ribosome is reading an mRNA and arrives at the codon UAA. Why does it stop adding amino acids?

options.label: A tRNA with the anticodon AUG binds and blocks the strand
The mRNA has simply run out of nucleotides at that spot
No tRNA recognizes that codon, so the ribosome knows the protein is finished
The small subunit cuts the strand and releases the large one

items.explain: No tRNA molecules recognize the stop codons, so the ribosome recognizes that translation is complete.

items.prompt: An antibiotic shuts down protein-making machinery in bacteria but leaves the patient's own cells working. What makes this possible?

options.label: Bacterial and human ribosomes differ in structure
Bacterial ribosomes are far larger than human ones
Human cells have no ribosomes of their own to harm
Bacterial ribosomes lack ribosomal RNA entirely

items.explain: Ribosomes differ in size, sequence and structure, so some antibiotics inhibit bacterial ribosomes while leaving human ribosomes unaffected.

items.prompt: A ribosome is reading one coding triplet in an mRNA. Which incoming tRNA delivers its amino acid?

options.label: Any tRNA nearby, since amino acids are chosen at random
The one carrying the amino acid used most often
Whichever tRNA is largest and binds first
The one whose anticodon matches that codon exactly

items.explain: For each codon there is a unique tRNA with the exact anticodon match, carrying the correct amino acid.

items.prompt: Biochemists notice that ribosomes inside mitochondria work more like bacterial ribosomes than like others in the same cell. What best explains this?

options.label: Mitochondria copy ribosomes from the nucleus and keep them unchanged
Mitochondria originated as bacteria living inside other cells
Bacteria in the cell lend their ribosomes to the mitochondria each day
Mitochondrial ribosomes are built from the cell's chloroplasts

items.explain: Mitoribosomes functionally resemble bacterial ones, reflecting the evolutionary origin of mitochondria as endosymbiotic bacteria.

items.prompt: Under a microscope, one mRNA strand has several ribosomes sitting on it at once. What are they doing?

options.label: Only the first reads it while the others wait their turn
Each is copying the strand into a new strand of DNA
Each is reading the strand and making its own protein molecule
They are breaking the strand down into nucleotides

items.explain: A polysome of two or more ribosomes can move along a single mRNA at one time, each producing a protein molecule.

items.prompt: A student adds a bacterial ribosome's 50S and 30S subunits and expects 80S, but the whole ribosome is 70S. What explains it?

options.label: Svedberg units measure sedimentation rate, not size, so they do not simply add
The two subunits lose part of their mass when they lock together
The mRNA strand takes up the missing 10 units between them
Each subunit is measured on a different scale of length

items.explain: The Svedberg unit measures the rate of sedimentation in centrifugation rather than size, so fragment names do not add up.
